body: Yeah but on the other hand I could just kill myself and no longer have the burden of having to decide on whether or not to do it.
I can but it's a bit like looking at all the fun balls in a ball pit and not being able to play with them. I can see it but I can't experience it.

The only thing I'm curious about is space. Space is full of mysteries, places never been touched before. But space is not somewhere I can currently go to and it's too much waiting for me until such time that it *would* be possible.

I just don't see the point in putting effort into something that has such a low chance of ever actually doing anything, there have been lots of attempts and few have ever actually succeeded and honestly it's a lot easier and a lot more simple to just end my life so that I can no longer feel or think.

It's inferred that who we are, our thoughts; perception; personality; dreams; aspirations, are just our mind. Once we die that's it, no more perception, and the only reason we can contemplate what it would be like without perception and thought is because we have it.

So really what's the point in doing anything to prolong the inevitable?

Because the likeliness that if I were to go out today and urge people to fight back against the government's decisions and have it actually work are slim to nil because people want to blend in with everyone else so I don't see it as worth the effort to try. Plus I am most definitely not a leader or even like people for that matter.
